comparison: Perfect agreement on experimental design claims (C5, C31-C33, C158-C162). Both evaluations find the comprehensive scope and methodological detail compelling and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes reproducibility details while peer reviewers highlight this as 'the largest and most comprehensive tissue respirometry analysis.'

Significant disagreement on methodological claims (C29-C30, C151-C153). OpenEval finds the method appropriately described with proper acknowledgment of limitations (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers express substantial concerns about the artificial nature of maximal respiration assays and emphasize data should be 'interpreted with caution' (UNCERTAIN).

Complete agreement on tissue-specific respiration patterns (C6, C36-C41). Both evaluations accept these descriptive findings as well-supported by the respirometry data, with peer reviewers describing evidence as 'compelling.'

Strong agreement on sex effects being modest (C7-C8, C43-C49, C122). Both evaluations accept the statistical evidence showing sex accounts for fewer significant differences than age. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative support (38 vs 90 differences) while peer reviewers summarize as 'sex has little influence.'

Strong agreement on age dominance (C9-C10, C50-C67, C77-C86, C93-C96). Both evaluations find comprehensive statistical support for age as the primary factor. OpenEval emphasizes multiple analytical approaches (PCA, correlation) while peer reviewers accept 'aging undermined mitochondrial function in most tissue' as a key finding.

Partial overlap with different emphasis. OpenEval addresses increased respiration claims (C51-C52, C60-C61, C130-C131, C143) and finds observations robust but compensatory interpretation speculative (UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers address broader heterogeneity claims (C11, C112-C119, C130-C131) including both increases and decreases, accepting all findings as SUPPORTED without questioning mechanistic interpretations.

OpenEval addresses age-related decreases in respiration (C52-C65, C102, C116-C117) finding them well-supported. Peer R6 addresses broader tissue heterogeneity including both increases and decreases (C11, C112-C119), accepting all patterns. Partial overlap on claims C116-C117 with agreement on support.

Perfect agreement on differential regulation of respiratory complexes (C97-C100). Both evaluations accept the summation analysis findings as supported, with peer reviewers incorporating this into the 'compelling' comprehensive dataset.
Complete agreement on sex-by-age interactions (C109-C111). Both evaluations accept the identification of tissue-specific divergent responses between males and females as supported by the data.

OpenEval addresses tissue resilience claims (C11, C118) finding them supported by kidney medulla example. Peer R6 addresses broader heterogeneity including resilience (C11, C112-C119), accepting all findings. Agreement on support with peer review covering wider claim set.

OpenEval addresses within-tissue heterogeneity (C42, C112-C115) finding it well-documented. Peer R6 addresses overlapping claims (C112-C115) as part of broader heterogeneity findings. Both evaluations find these patterns supported.

OpenEval specifically addresses multivariate analyses (C93-C95) as independent confirmation of age dominance. Peer R5 includes these claims within comprehensive age-effect evaluation. Both find the statistical approaches supporting age as dominant factor.

Agreement on comparison to transcriptomic studies (C120-C121). OpenEval finds concordance strengthens findings though comparison is qualitative (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept interpretation and note study provides 'foundational knowledge' for the field (SUPPORTED).

OpenEval addresses mechanistic link between transcriptomics and function (C128-C129) finding it plausible but speculative (UNCERTAIN). Peer R10 addresses broader speculative claims (C125-C129, C145-C147, C157) accepting them as reasonable interpretations (SUPPORTED). Disagreement on level of certainty for mechanistic inferences.

Significant disagreement on compensatory mechanism claims (C145-C147). OpenEval finds these speculative and requiring additional experiments (UNSUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept as reasonable speculation, noting discussion is 'descriptive and cautious' (SUPPORTED). Different standards for speculative mechanistic claims.

Partial overlap on methodological limitations. OpenEval addresses caveats about methodology (C150, C154-C157) finding them appropriate (SUPPORTED). Peer R2 emphasizes similar limitations (C151-C155) but with greater concern about interpretation (UNCERTAIN). Different emphasis on severity of limitations.

Agreement on cell-type limitation (C156). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers acknowledge that bulk tissue measurements may mask cell-type-specific differences as an inherent limitation of the approach (SUPPORTED).

OpenEval identifies lack of justification for mouse-to-human age conversions (C34-C35) as uncertain due to missing citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.
